description: Regulated cloud migration proposal for a member-owned regional credit union.
provenance: Modeled on cloud transformation proposals for regulated financial institutions: migration factory scope, landing-zone controls, application waves, resilience targets, economic model, regulatory evidence, and fixed-fee terms. Deliberately exercises a nine-slide deck with a three-series line chart and detailed risk-control language.

document.presentationTitle: Cloud Migration Proposal — Harborview Credit Union

content.title: Cloud Migration Proposal
content.subtitle: Prepared for Harborview Credit Union | September 15, 2026 | Proposal ACA-2026-119

content.title: A 20-month migration exits both data centers before renewal.
content.subtitle: Executive recommendation
prose: Scope migrates 86 applications to a dual-region Azure platform.
The core mainframe and two card interfaces remain on dedicated connectivity.
Altura owns delivery from landing zone through cutover and 90 days of hypercare.

content.title: Case for change
content.subtitle: Findings from architecture, operations, and regulatory discovery
bulletPoints: Primary and recovery data-center leases expire in June and September 2028; renewal would require a five-year commitment
Thirty-two percent of Windows servers reach end of support by October 2027 and 19 applications depend on unsupported middleware
The 2026 recovery test restored tier-one services in 11.4 hours versus the board-approved eight-hour objective
Infrastructure changes require six manual approvals across separate tools, with incomplete linkage to affected assets
Current hosting spend of $18.9M annually grows 7% under signed colocation, hardware, and software commitments
NCUA examiners requested stronger evidence of privileged-access review and recovery testing for member-facing systems

content.subtitle: Annual hosting and transformation cash cost, $M

content.title: Migration waves and exit milestones
content.subtitle: Twenty months from notice to proceed
bulletPoints: Months 1-3 — landing zone, dedicated connectivity, identity integration, control library, and regulator evidence plan
Months 4-6 — Wave 1: development tooling, collaboration, and low-risk internal applications
Months 7-10 — Wave 2: data platform and member analytics; Wave 3: lending support and document services
Months 11-15 — Wave 4: online banking dependencies, payments support, and enterprise integration services
Months 16-18 — Wave 5: remaining tier-one systems, full recovery exercise, and disaster-recovery cutover
Months 19-20 — data-center decommission, license true-down, evidence binder, and 90-day hypercare commencement

content.title: Investment and commercial model
content.subtitle: Fixed-fee delivery with shared migration contingencies
bulletPoints: Program fee — $14.8M fixed for landing zone, migration factory, 86 applications, testing, and hypercare
Cloud consumption — estimated $8.1M in FY2027 and $13.7M in FY2028 under reserved-capacity assumptions
Third-party remediation allowance — $2.6M controlled by Harborview; unused funds remain with Harborview
Milestone holdback — 15% of program fees payable only after recovery proof and data-center exit acceptance
Schedule commitment — Altura funds incremental delivery labor if the June 2028 exit date is missed for provider-controlled reasons
Change control — application count and complexity bands fixed after the first 45-day validation sprint

content.title: Authorize validation by October 30 to protect the exit date.
content.subtitle: Proposed decision path
prose: Altura delivers the wave baseline, control matrix, and fixed-fee schedule in 45 days.
Harborview may stop after validation for a capped fee of $620,000.
